name: RevengeHotels
iocPatterns: Spear-phishing with macro-laden documents or malicious script files
Redirects to fraudulent document storage websites (e.g., hosting sites used as staging)
Use of RAT families such as VenomRAT and GodRAT for persistent C2
Social engineering lures regarding job applications, invoices, and reservation details
keyCapabilities: Remote Access Trojan (RAT) deployment and management
Malware distribution via fraudulent cloud storage links
Evasion of security controls to maintain long-term persistence in hospitality networks
recommendedActions: Implement advanced email filtering to block malicious links and known-malicious file types (.scr, .exe).
Deploy an Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solution specifically tuned to alert on RAT behaviors.
Isolate hotel front desk systems from the primary corporate network using VLAN segmentation.
Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all staff access points and guest portals.
Conduct targeted phishing awareness training focusing on 'scam' invoice/job offer lures for hospitality staff.
Perform regular security audits of any hosted document storage sites used by employees or guests.
Implement a rigid blocklist for known malicious domains associated with fraudulent document hosting.
Monitor network traffic for non-standard communication from front-desk workstations to external IPs.
campaignsText: RevengeHotels has shown a consistent operational focus on the hospitality industry for over a decade. A notable progression in their tactics was observed when they transitioned from community-centric distribution (such as Skype-based files) to targeted, high-conversion phishing campaigns using fraudulent document hosting sites. Between June and August 2025, a specific surge was noted targeting Brazil and Spain. The actor maintains a steady operational tempo, regularly updating its RAT offerings—most recently integrating VenomRAT—to maintain reliable access to victim networks.
description: RevengeHotels (TA558) is a persistent cybercrime actor targeting the hospitality, tourism, and travel industries since at least 2015. The group specializes in stealing credit card data from hotel guests by deploying remote access trojans (RATs) like VenomRAT and GodRAT via sophisticated social engineering and phishing campaigns.
goals: The primary objective of RevengeHotels is financial gain through the theft of personally identifiable information (PII) and payment card industry (PCI) data. They specifically target the hospitality sector because these organizations process high volumes of credit card transactions for thousands of diverse travelers every day. By compromising hotel front desks, the actor can harvest guest data at scale. Their targeting also extends to other high-value sectors like financial services and infrastructure when there is a secondary opportunity for profit or data monetization.
